page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) operating at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 1344.0 GB, yielding 84.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, reflecting the high 4.2 GHz clock speed of the Intel Xeon processor. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also register strong performance in the top 25% tier. Large-block memory write bandwidth is measured at 91.75 GB/sec, which is also in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance, database operations, and Redis SET operations fall within the average range, indicating that while parallel scaling is moderate due to the 16-vCPU limit, individual thread execution is highly efficient.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX64-16mds_v2 offers high resource density specifically tailored for memory-bound applications. The extreme RAM-to-vCPU ratio allows organizations to host massive datasets in-memory without paying for unnecessary extra CPU cores. This makes the instance highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy data analytics, enterprise relational databases, and memory-intensive simulation workloads that benefit from high single-core CPU speeds and fast local NVMe storage.
